newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Indo-Bangladesh joint committee on Ganges water monitoring began its first inspection meeting yesterday at small north-western town of Bheramara.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria yesterday said the government was determined to denationalise the loss-incurring induistries.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said yesterday the killer of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman must be tried and the process of trial has started. She said protectors of the killers had violated human rights.

Gas supply remained cut off for almost the whole day yesterday affecting household work in some parts of Dhaka city. Meanwhile, uncertainty is looming large over the prospects of Irri-Boro cultivation in Rajshahi and other northern districts as shortage of power supply has rendered many deep and shallow tubewells inoperative, affecting irrigation.

Rebel faction of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (student wing of opposition BNP party) confined its president Shahiduddin Chowdhury Ani and general seceretary Habib-un Nabi Sohel into the guest room of Suryasen Hall of the Dhaka University for three hours on Thursday demanding dismissal of the recently announced JDC convening committee.
Police will begin house to house search in a couple of days to recover unauthorised arms under a special drive to improve the law and order.
The World Bank has reiterated its continued support to reform programmes in different agreed sectors of the economy in Bnagladesh, report BSS (the official news agency).
